notes: Company: mid-market product analytics SaaS, heavy interactive UI with embedded chat + search
Primary motivation: reduce token cost on frequent KB lookups and guarantee tail latency during peak support hours
Customer quote: "Need predictable bills for support feature - spikes during release windows kill margins."
Initial fit: good for Hosted API to validate prompt set; moving to Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation
Security: requires SSO (SAML), SOC2, audit logs to integrate with internal SIEM; must support KMS for key rotation
POC goals (success criteria): p95 latency < 350ms for chat single-turn; end-to-end reranking accuracy delta <= 2% vs baseline; 30% token cost reduction via batching/caching
POC dataset: 2k representative KB queries + 400 annotated rerank pairs provided by customer (shared via Drive)
Traffic profile: 70% short queries (<=128 tokens), 30% long context (>=512 tokens); peak concurrent sessions target ~200 requests/sec
Cost sensitivity: concerned about variable token spend during promotions; leaning toward reserved capacity if committed pricing reduces unit cost
Model preferences: prefers open-weight Llama-family variants initially; willing to test quantized variants if quality maintained
Routing/fallback requirements: need automatic fallback to smaller cheaper variant under overload, and region failover from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 -> eu-west-1
Canary plan (agreed): week 1 small traffic canary (5% traffic) on Dedicated pool using model-variant-v1, monitor 48h; week 2 expand to 25% if metrics stable; full cutover after 7 days stable
Canary metrics to watch: error rate, p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, top-5 quality regressions on eval set
Fallback/rollback triggers: error rate > 1.5% sustained 10m OR p95 latency > 2x baseline OR top-5 quality regression > 5% -> automatic rollback to previous variant + route to hosted fallback
Region failover plan: primary us-east-1, async replication of prefix cache to us-west-2; health-check interval 30s, failover TTL 5m; manual verification step for eu-west-1 enablement
Observability: want token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and prompt-level traces; Redwood Console dashboards requested
Integration notes: will use VPC peering and private endpoints; internal networking team requires NAT/egress audit logs
Open legal blocker: customer requires limited data residency clause in SOW for EU customer vectors (affects rollout to EU region)
Pricing conversation: Redwood proposed 3-month Dedicated trial (2 x A100 equiv) + usage overage; customer requested alternate with flat-per-month cap
